quick_skim.title: Repository-Level Solidity Code Generation with Large Language Models: From Prompting to Fine-Tuning
quick_skim.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in general-purpose code generation, but their effectiveness in specialized software domains remains underexplored. Solidity smart contracts represent a high-stakes domain where generated code must satisfy strict language-level, security, and software-engineering constraints. Existing benchmarks and metrics remain insufficient for repository-level Solidity generation, where models must synthesize complete contracts from natural language requirements. To address this gap, we introduce SolidityBench, a benchmark of 5,470 repository-level Solidity smart contracts paired with natural language descriptions. We also propose SolidityScore, a Solidity-aware semantic metric that emphasizes domain-critical constructs such as security modifiers, contract declarations, and Solidity-specific keywords. Using this benchmark, we evaluate representative code LLMs, including Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, and CodeLlama, across zero-shot prompting, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, in-context learning, retrieval-augmented generation, and supervised fine-tuning. The results show that general-purpose models exhibit systematic structural deficiencies in repository-level Solidity generation. Among non-parametric methods, retrieval-augmented generation performs best, while in-context learning degrades beyond two examples due to context saturation. Supervised fine-tuning achieves the largest improvement by internalizing Solidity-specific constraints into model parameters. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive benchmark for repository-level Solidity code generation and shows that high-quality domain data combined with supervised fine-tuning is the most effective strategy for improving the reliability of LLM-generated smart contracts.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Introduces SolidityBench, a benchmark of 5,470 repository-level Solidity smart contracts with natural language descriptions, and SolidityScore, a semantic metric for evaluating generated code.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 大型语言模型在通用代码生成上表现出色，但在Solidity等专业领域效果未知，且缺乏仓库级生成基准。本文提出SolidityBench，包含5470个仓库级Solidity智能合约及其自然语言描述，以及SolidityScore语义度量。该工作为Solidity代码生成提供标准化评估，促进领域特定代码生成研究。
